transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (NovaHealth Head of ML), Ethan Cole (NovaHealth Infra Eng), Marta Silva (NovaHealth CTO)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs NovaHealth's baseline provider (BaselineCloud), discuss tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization), and agree next steps for on-prem evaluation and pricing. Medium transcription quality; some names slightly off.

Topics:
- Benchmark numbers (p50/p95 latency, throughput/tokens per second)
- Differences vs baseline provider (BaselineCloud): latency tradeoffs, model variants, cost per token
- Tuning recommendations: batching, KV cache, quantization profile, route fallbacks
- Operational requirements: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SSO
- Next steps and action items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight for 45-ish minutes. Diego and I will run through the benchmark slides and then take Qs. Priya, Marta, Ethan, thanks for being here.
[00:18] Priya (NovaHealth): Thanks, Laura. We got your last run earlier today. Quick note, some of the headers were truncated, but we got the gist.
[00:27] Diego (Redwood SE): Cool. I'll share my screen, give me one sec. The run we're discussing is the 4k context runs, mixed q4fb quant profile, and two routing configs: dedicated dedicated-1 and hosted-fallback. Some transcripts earlier labeled it "read wood dedicated" in the doc, ignore that.
[00:48] Marta (NovaHealth): Got it. We're mostly focused on p95 tail and the cost delta vs BaselineCloud. Our SLO is 250ms p95 for the 1k typical route, and for larger contexts 1.2s is acceptable.
[01:05] Diego (Redwood SE): Perfect so first slide, p50/p95 numbers for the 1k and 4k prompt sets. For 1k, Redwood Dedicated p50 = 48ms, p95 = 180ms. BaselineCloud p50 = 42ms, p95 = 290ms. For 4k, Redwood p50 = 210ms, p95 = 980ms; BaselineCloud p50 = 230ms, p95 = 1.4s.
[01:36] Ethan (NovaHealth): Wait, BaselineCloud p95 is that high for 4k? Are those runs with KV cache enabled?
[01:43] Diego (Redwood SE): The BaselineCloud numbers were from the spreadsheet you sent if I recall their runs didn't use an efficient KV prefix cache, they were cold-start heavy. Our runs had KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes, that shaves about 30-40% off p95 on the long context.
[02:01] Laura (Redwood AE): Also worth pointing out throughput: we saw sustained throughput at 120 tokens/sec per GPU for the Redwood Dedicated config under the mixed workload, and BaselineCloud reported 85 tokens/sec.
[02:15] Priya (NovaHealth): Those per-GPU numbers are interesting. How did you handle batching? Baseline tends to batch aggressively which can help throughput but hurts latency.
[02:24] Diego (Redwood SE): Right our batch policy is workload-aware: aggressive batching only on background routes, conservative on low-latency routes. For these numbers the p95 is measured under conservative latency SLOs, so we limit max batch size to 8 and prioritize older requests.
[02:40] Marta (NovaHealth): And memory/VRAM usage? We have concerns about 80GB A100 availability in our on-prem racks.
[02:48] Diego (Redwood SE): The quant profile q4fb reduces memory; peak VRAM for the 4k run was about 42GB per model shard. On smaller context it's closer to 22-26GB. If you have 80GB cards you'll be fine even for multi-model sharding.
[03:03] Ethan (NovaHealth): Ok that's helpful. One challenge is our network egress to hosted endpoints we may need a VPC peering or private link.
[03:11] Laura (Redwood AE): We documented VPC options in the security pack; Diego we'll re-attach that. We also have a Private option where control plane is customer-managed, which sounds like what NovaHealth wants for production.
[03:24] Priya (NovaHealth): On quality, small question: did you run the same prompt set as our baseline? We sent a 200 prompt test set with QA scoring.
[03:33] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes; we reused your 200 prompt QA set plus a 3k conversational anchor set. Quality deltas were nil between models at same weights the main differences were latency and cost. We did see one regression on long-chain reasoning which we flagged (example 87) likely tokenization edge-case with the quant profile.
[03:54] Marta (NovaHealth): Can you correlate that regression with quantization? We can't accept quality regressions above 1% on our pass rate.
[04:03] Diego (Redwood SE): We're on it action item to run the failing prompt with q8_0 and float16 path to compare. If the regression persists it's a model tokenization issue, not Redwood infra.
[04:18] Priya (NovaHealth): Good. Back to cost what's the delta per 1M tokens between Redwood Dedicated vs BaselineCloud hosted?
[04:27] Laura (Redwood AE): Roughly, at the committed capacity pricing we modeled, Redwood Dedicated operational cost is about 18% lower per token for your workload profile when you account for KV cache and batching savings. BaselineCloud list price looked cheaper but when you factor in extra tail latency and lower batching efficiency, your unit economics favored Dedicated. We'll send the spreadsheet.
[04:49] Ethan (NovaHealth): Can you explain the 'fallback to hosted' bit? If dedicated is saturated do you route to a cheaper hosted model?
[04:57] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, smart routing can failover by policy. For NovaHealth the plan was: primary is Dedicated (pinned model v1.2), fallback to Hosted-compatible variant with same weights, and a final fallback to a smaller quantized variant if cost SLO triggers. That preserves availability at degraded latency.
[05:14] Priya (NovaHealth): And audit/compliance do you capture token-level logs and provide audit trails? We need immutable audit with KMS wrapping.
[05:21] Laura (Redwood AE): Yes, we provide audit logs, KMS integration for payload encryption, and SOC2 evidence in the security pack. For Private installs we can support HSM integrations.
[05:33] Marta (NovaHealth): Excellent. One more ops question: can you run benchmarks inside our data center hardware? We'd like to see runs on our exact 80GB A100s.
[05:42] Diego (Redwood SE): Absolutely. We can run the on-prem evaluation; need access to a test subnet and at least one node with your standard config. We'll bring a small benchmarking harness and run the same scripts you used for baseline.
[05:53] Priya (NovaHealth): Great. Timeline: if we get results this week and the pricing sheet, we can align stakeholders for a decision next week.
[05:59] Laura (Redwood AE): Sounds reasonable. Quick caveat: some of the numbers you have from BaselineCloud were self-reported; we recommend a side-by-side run in your infra for apples-to-apples.
[06:10] Ethan (NovaHealth): Understood.
[06:13] Diego (Redwood SE): One more technical note we measured seq-latency improvements when enabling prefix KV cache, particularly for repeated system prompts. That cut p95 by around 35% on the 4k conversational anchor. We should include a run with cold cache too so you can see worst-case.
[06:31] Priya (NovaHealth): Yes please. The worst-case matters for compliance.
[06:35] Marta (NovaHealth): Also, what about HH latency under encryption? Any CPU overhead for payload encryption at scale?
[06:44] Diego (Redwood SE): Minimal; modern KMS + TLS stack overhead is in the sub-1% latency for per-request encryption. The heavier cost is network hop. If you colocate, that overhead drops.
[06:56] Laura (Redwood AE): Ok let's recap next steps. Diego will share raw logs and a runbook; I'll send pricing and Dedicated sizing options; Priya will share final QA threshold doc; Ethan will provide network topology and test access. We'll aim for the on-prem run next week.
[07:20] Priya (NovaHealth): Thanks, team. One small ask can you include the exact kernel/k8s configs used? There was a mismatch last time.
[07:28] Diego (Redwood SE): Yep docker images, kernel flags, and our kernel selection table will be included.
[07:33] Marta (NovaHealth): Perfect.
[07:36] Laura (Redwood AE): Any other questions?
[07:38] Ethan (NovaHealth): None from infra.
[07:40] Priya (NovaHealth): All good.
[07:42] Laura (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.
[07:46] Diego (Redwood SE): Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
